correctness.rationale: Every subgroup outside an odd generalized-dihedral kernel is uniquely H(B,x)=B⋊<xt> with x taken modulo B. Kernel subgroups are normal. For two outside subgroups, explicit multiplication shows permutability is equivalent to x-y lying in B+C because A/(B+C) has odd order. The exact number of compatible coset pairs is |A:B∩C|, giving the stated numerator. For elementary abelian kernels, the standard subspace-intersection count gives eta exactly. Leading exponents of the Gaussian sums were optimized under all feasible dimensions, including the rank-one boundary case.

value.rationale: Subgroup commutativity degree is a natural probabilistic invariant of subgroup lattices. The theorem replaces the ordinary dihedral cyclic kernel by every finite odd abelian kernel and compresses the full answer to three intrinsic lattice sums. The elementary-abelian specialization then reveals a nontrivial parity phase transition—limit 1/4 in fixed even rank versus decay 3/p in fixed odd rank at least three—giving structural information not visible from a routine single-family substitution.
